title: Tokyo's Akihabara Gets Solar-Powered Trash Cans
paragraphs: Tourists love visiting Japan for its history, food and more. But there's one thing many tourists don't love: there aren't many trash cans!
This isn't just a problem for tourists. In the last few years, popular neighborhoods in Tokyo and other cities have seen an increase in trash on the streets.

However, it's not as easy as just putting a few trash cans on the corner. Local governments have found that these trash cans quickly overflow as they're used by both people on the street and people in nearby homes, and it can be expensive to keep emptying them.
One solution is to make trash cans that don't fill up so quickly. And one neighborhood in Tokyo is trying a high-tech solution.
Akihabara, known as one of the best places in Tokyo for technology, has put 22 solar-powered SmaGo trash cans in 10 places around the area.

These trash cans can hold much more trash than normal ones, because they can compact the trash to a fifth of its size. They also have an online system that lets workers check how full each can is, so they know when it needs to be emptied.
The trash cans come from a Tokyo tech company called Forcetec.
Akihabara isn't the first place to get SmaGo trash cans. They're already found in other parts of Tokyo, as well as neighborhoods in Osaka, Kyoto and other prefectures.
But it's the first time a local government in Japan has put so many of these trash cans in one place. And Akihabara hopes they'll help keep the neighborhood clean!
